column5: The canonical buffer, optional middle-cache, and snapshot merge is retained unchanged and now receives the injected MemBufferDriver as the live transaction buffer; precedence, tombstone suppression, missing-key fallback, commit timestamps, and source error identity execute, while context, client-go not-found conversion, map-plus-error results, and concrete TiKV reads remain external.

The injected mutable buffer and snapshot create forward and reverse iterators through the sole TransactionReadDriver and UnionIter path with exact error propagation and cleanup; concrete txnsnapshot.Scanner construction and extractKeyErr conversion still require the external TiKV client.

Get, BatchGet, Iter, IterReverse, and replacement snapshot interception remain connected to the canonical mutable transaction; concrete KVSnapshot ownership and isolation, priority, replica, runtime-stat, RPC, resource-group, timeout, and scan-size option projection remain external.

TransactionReadDriver now consumes MemBufferDriver directly for dirty-first Get, canonical BatchGet, Set, Delete, forward and reverse union scans, snapshot interception, and prefix deletion without a second transaction model. Commit, locking, table metadata, checkpoints, the complete option registry, key-exists publication, fair locking, pipelined flushing, KV filtering, context, pair-result shapes, and a concrete TiKV transaction remain open.

The complete source-owned forward and reverse dirty-snapshot merge remains the sole iterator authority and is covered by the exact TestUnionIter and TestUnionIterErrors transfers: dirty precedence, tombstones, equal-key advancement, either input exhausting first, originating error identity, constructor failure ownership, and close-both behavior are all retained; the injected MemBufferDriver supplies its live upstream without making broader transaction gaps part of this source owner's status.

MemBufferDriver is a direct generic adapter over an injected MemBufferBackend, not an invented database. It owns live Get and BatchGet, Set and Delete tombstones, typed flags and assertions, remove, local reads, staging cleanup/release/inspection, ordered live iteration, stable snapshot getter/iteration, and pipelined-DML empty snapshot views. Concrete client-go MemDB, client flag-bit and error conversion, memory sizing equivalence, and backend concurrency remain external.

The previously covered ScanMetaWithPrefix, DelKeyWithPrefix, and RowKeyPrefixFilter authority is retained unchanged and now executes against the canonical MemBufferDriver-backed transaction; exact PrefixNext bounds, defensive prefix checks, iterator closure, stop semantics, key cloning before mutation, tombstones, and embedded-NUL filtering remain covered.
